Dev report — audited sweep complete. **No PR: the sweep found zero defects to fix, and forcing one would be fabrication.** The dispatch premise (roughly 16 incoherent doubles remain unswept and need fixing) is falsified; the card's underlying *class* premise is confirmed as history.

## The denominator, and how it was derived

Audited at `2473cd2d3` (fast-forwarded mid-task — `packages/objectql` moved under me and added a double, so the whole audit was re-derived rather than reported stale).

**Enumeration (the set I searched):** every object literal in `packages/objectql/src/**/*.ts` carrying at least 3 data-access members AND at least one write verb (`update`/`delete`/`updateMany`/`deleteMany`/`bulkUpdate`/`bulkDelete`/`upsert`), found with the TypeScript compiler API — not grep, so the set does not depend on a spelling.

| | count |
|---|---|
| literals matched by the enumerator | 156 |
| − production source (`engine.ts:463` — not a double) | 1 |
| − call-counter object false-positived (`engine-write-not-found-gate.test.ts:133` — members named like write verbs, values are numbers) | 1 |
| − bench file, not run by `vitest run` (`engine-data-events.bench.ts:54`; audited statically, read side answers) | 1 |
| **genuine test doubles audited behaviourally** | **153** |

For scale: triage's 17:59Z starting count was 23 `findOne: async () => null` sites. That grep still returns exactly 23 — my predicate is strictly broader and reaches 153.

## The predicate I actually swept for, and what it misses

I did **not** sweep for `findOne: async () => null`. The property is *the read side cannot answer for the rows the write side touches*, so I measured it behaviourally: instrument every double, record every call with the arguments it was handed **and the value its reads returned**, then for each by-id `update`/`delete` of id X ask whether that same double's `findOne` ever answered a row for X.

Static classification (`always-empty` / `id-blind` / `answers`) was only used to pick what to look at; the verdicts below are runtime.

**What it still misses**, stated plainly: it can only see incoherence that the **current suite exercises**. A double that is incoherent but never handed a by-id write is invisible to a behavioural probe by construction — which is why the dormant population is reported separately below rather than folded into "clean".

## Live-vs-dormant probe (the #7620 methodology)

Instrumented all 153 doubles by splicing a recording Proxy around each literal via a Vite transform, keyed to the AST offsets. **Control: the instrumented suite ran 192 files / 3400 tests, all green** — the probe perturbs nothing — and recorded **24,385 calls**.

Two dead-probe failures were caught and fixed *by the control*, which is the only reason the silence below is evidence:

1. First run reported 17 doubles with **zero** calls. Not dormancy — my writer buffered 400 records and flushed on `process.on('exit')`, which never fires in vitest workers, so every worker under the threshold silently lost its whole buffer. Fixed to flush per call; the 17 dropped to 1.
2. Instrumenting all 153 (rather than only the flagged subset) turned **6 tests red**. Not a discovery — my wrapper cache was keyed by property name, so a double whose member is reassigned mid-test (`driver.findOne = …`) kept serving a wrapper around the stale function. Re-keyed by the underlying function; suite green again.

## Verdict per member

| verdict | count | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **live-incoherent (fixed)** | **0** | no double anywhere took a by-id write its own read side denied |
| **id-blind read side** | **0** | no double answered a constant row regardless of the id asked for |
| coherent under a real by-id write | **63** | took at least one by-id write; read side answered for every one (0 denied, 0 unread) — the **positive control** proving the instrument distinguishes answered from denied |
| called, never handed a by-id write | **89** | of these, **37** statically carry a read side that denies every row; their incoherence is real but **dormant** |
| never called at all | **1** | `engine-driver-registration.test.ts:45` — its own comment says "only identity/name/version matter here" |
| deliberately skipped | **0** | see the #8080 note below |

**Not one of the 37 statically-incoherent doubles takes a by-id write.** That is the sweep's whole result.

## The live sibling claim: not contended

**#8080's file was audited and needed no edit.** `search-companion-read-projection-conformance.test.ts:126` took 2 by-id writes and its read side answered both — verdict *coherent*. So the skip clause never fired, and I made no edit in that file. #8118 and #7168 never intersected the enumerated set.

## Why zero — the part worth more than the fixes would have been

The card says the five found by #7867/#7989 were found by coincidence, and "that is not a discovery mechanism". True of how they were found — but **PR #7989 turned it into one**. It did not merely fix five doubles; it made the by-id prior-row read **unconditional**. From that commit on, a driver-shaped double whose `findOne` denies the row fails loudly with `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` the moment anyone points a by-id write at it. So the green suite is positive evidence that no driver-shaped incoherence is load-bearing — not merely an absence of evidence. The same holds for engine-shaped doubles at `protocol.updateData`/`deleteData` via #4435's existence probe.

Both seams are already pinned, which is why I added no pin — every candidate I drafted duplicated one of these:

- `engine-write-not-found-gate.test.ts` (all three write faces), plus the read-count pins in `engine-update-prior-read-scope.test.ts` / `engine-delete-prior-read-scope.test.ts` that pin the read as *unconditional*;
- `protocol-data.test.ts` "updateData refuses an id that names no row" (`code: RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, `status: 404`) and `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.record-not-found.test.ts` for the `delete` twin.

Adding a third assertion of the same property would be churn, so the honest deliverable is the audit plus the follow-on.

## Gates

- `pnpm check:engine-double-contract` — **green, before and after, unchanged**: `OK — 175 pinned, 133 in the DEBT ledger, 2 exempt`. (I changed none of the doubles it pins, which is why it is unchanged rather than merely green.)
- `pnpm check:query-options-erasure` — green: `67 unswept non-test site(s) in 17 file(s), none new`; baseline key set verified, no files added.
- `pnpm check:type-check-debt --re-measure` — **not run, and deliberately not**: it refuses without a full built closure, and my diff is **empty** (`git status --porcelain` clean, zero commits ahead of `main`), so a re-measure would measure `main`, not a change of mine. The `+N` drift you warned about needs touched test files; I touched none. Flagging rather than silently skipping.

## Follow-on filed

**#8194** (`finding`, `domain:devx`, unassigned) carries the full audit data for the gate-widening decision — including the measurement that most changes its cost: the obvious static predicate flags **37** doubles in objectql alone, **none** of them a defect, so a naive widening ships a 37-entry exceptions ledger on day one, in one package. It argues both sides and names the alternative the data supports (pin the *seams*, which are a small decidable set, rather than the doubles).

## ACCEPTED and CLOSED — the sweep ran, the answer is **zero**, and no code change was warranted.

Engine-core seat #6019, `session_014C8pAprWdmtecFsEprZax4`. ⛔ **`premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is the delivery here, not a failed dispatch.** The card asked for an *audited sweep*; the audit **is** the product, and it came back negative.

### The acceptance bar was the denominator, and it was met by a wide margin

I said I would send this back for the denominator alone. Instead of a hit-list:

- **156 literals enumerated by AST**, minus one production-source literal, one call-counter false positive and one bench-file double ⇒ **153 genuine doubles**, each named rather than counted.
- **Every one instrumented at runtime**, with **24,385 calls** recorded — arguments *and* return values.

| verdict | count |
|---|---|
| took a by-id `update`/`delete` its own read side **denied** | **0** |
| had an id-blind read side | **0** |
| took a real by-id write and was **answered** (positive control) | **63** |
| called, never handed a by-id write — of which **37** statically carry an always-empty read side, **dormantly** | **89** |
| never called | **1** |

⭐ The **63** matter as much as the zero: without a positive control, "no incoherence found" is indistinguishable from an instrument that cannot tell answered from denied.

### ⭐ The root cause of the zero is worth more than the fixes would have been

The card's framing was that the five doubles fixed in PR #7989 were found by coincidence, and *"the next incoherent double waits for the next unrelated change."* **The sweep falsifies the second half.**

#7989 did not merely fix five doubles — it installed the **unconditional** by-id prior-row read, which turned the whole class **self-detecting at the engine seam**: a driver-shaped double whose `findOne` denies the row now fails its own test loudly with `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` the moment anyone points a by-id write at it. #4435 does the same at `protocol.updateData`/`deleteData`.

⇒ **The green suite is now evidence, not merely an absence of evidence.** And since both seams are already pinned, every pin the dev drafted duplicated an existing one — so it **added none**. ⛔ Adding a redundant pin to have something to show is the failure mode that was correctly avoided.

⚠️ Note what closed this card: **work this same lane landed today**. #7867 → #7989 was dispatched five hours before #8058 was, and it dissolved #8058's premise as a side effect nobody predicted at dispatch time.

### ⭐ The probe caught itself being dead — twice

The methodology I asked it to reuse (#7620's live-vs-dormant control) was applied to the instrument itself, and the full-suite control (192 files / 3400 tests green **with all 153 doubles wrapped**) caught two dead-probe failures:

1. a **buffered writer** lost every worker under the flush threshold — **17 doubles falsely read as "never called"**, dropping to 1 after a per-call flush;
2. a **wrapper cache keyed by property name** served a stale function to tests that reassign a member mid-run — 6 tests red, green after re-keying by the underlying function.

⛔ Either would have produced a confident, wrong sweep. This is the difference between a measurement and a number.

### One correction owed, and it is exactly the kind precision demands

⚠️ The report says **153** doubles; **#8194 says 154**. The denominator is this card's whole acceptance bar, so the two must agree. ⛔ Not a rework — the sweep's conclusion is unaffected either way — but **please reconcile the figure on #8194**, since that card carries the number forward as the input to a gate-design decision.

### Disposition

**Closed `completed`**: the deliverable was an audited sweep, it was delivered, and the finding is answered — the class is enforced behaviourally at both consumer seams and no incoherent double is load-bearing.

**#8194 carries the class forward** to `domain:devx`, exactly as the ruling planned — and it starts from data rather than from the hypothesis. ⭐ Its most valuable content is the one the sweep could only have learned by running: the distinguishing predicate is *"does the write side get addressed by id at all"*, which is a **runtime** property, so the obvious static gate flags **37 correct doubles in one package** and would ship a 37-entry exceptions ledger on day one. It proposes inverting the subject — pin the **seams**, not the doubles — and says plainly that this is a different gate from the one its own title proposes.
